podcast.title: Compromised Audio Processing in iPhones
podcast.body: Even high-end iPhones, costing upwards of 1000 euros, are noted for having a "disappointing" sound processing chip. This reflects Apple's historical design philosophy for its portable devices, prioritizing features like screen, processor, and battery over dedicated audio quality. This approach, inherited from the early iPods, has set a standard in the portable electronics market where sound processing is not a primary concern for manufacturers. "aunque tú te cojas un un iPhone de mil euros y tú te mira es el chip de procesado de sonido que tiene es cuanto menos decepcionante."

podcast.title: Mac 4 Boot Sound (Early 90s)
podcast.body: Jim Riggs, Apple's sound designer, created the welcome sound for the Mac 4, launched in the early 1990s. This sound was inspired by the final chord of The Beatles' song "A Day in the Life" and, with minor tonal variations, has been used in most Macs to the present day. "diseñó la bienvenida, inspirada en la cor de final de una de los mejores temas de los Beatles, Adegin de Life."

podcast.title: iPod - Design Philosophy Shift
podcast.body: The Apple iPod, while bringing fantastic innovations, introduced design flaws and conceptual problems that continue to affect portable devices like smartphones today. Although inspired by the Creative Nomad Jukebox, the iPod was not the first MP3 player with a hard drive. Apple's version prioritized making the device smaller, lighter, with better battery life, and more user-friendly. This came at the cost of audio quality, as its sound processing chip was significantly less powerful than that of the Nomad Jukebox. Apple's focus on portability and affordability over pristine audio fidelity became the dominant philosophy, shaping how sound is processed in most portable gadgets today, including modern iPhones, where even expensive models often feature disappointing audio processing chips. "el iPod de Apple no fue el primer reproductor MP3 con disco duró no fue realmente hubo un reproductor MP3 con disco duró anterior al iPod que fue este el creativ no man jukebox que tenía seis gigas de disco duro y fue el primer reproductor de alta capacidad que usaba disco duro y no usaba memoria flash esta máquina fue en la que se inspiró a Apple para hacer el iPod."
